name: Tabs
summary: Tabs are a strip of buttons over one box of content, with a single panel showing at a time. Use them to swap between views of the same thing without leaving the page. The strip is one Tab stop and the arrow keys move inside it, so the panel underneath has to be somewhere the keyboard can still land.
demoNote: Everything under Common mistakes is live, and each failing strip sits beside a correct one because the two are indistinguishable to look at. Every readout is measured by asking the browser which elements it will really give focus to.

contract.useWhen: Swap panels in place. Not for moving between pages; that is jump-nav.
keyboard: one stop for the strip, then into the panel
native: selects the focused tab. Under automatic activation the arrow already did
move and select, since the panels are already in the DOM
the same, and the only pair that moves, when the strip is vertical
states: vertical — aria-orientation=vertical on the tablist, which swaps which arrows move
failureModes: every tab at tabindex=0, so the strip is as many stops as it has tabs
unselected panels hidden with opacity, which hides them from nobody — their links are still stops
no tabindex on the panel, so Tab steps over it and its name is never read
links wearing role=tab, announcing as a widget while aria-controls names panels nobody built
api: AC.createTabs(root, options) -> { select, selected, tabs, panels, destroy }
